venue.name: Alert Bay Public Library & Museum
venue.description: Alert Bay Public Library & Museum is a community library and local history museum on Cormorant Island, run by the Alert Bay Public Library and Museum Association, which was incorporated in 1958. The library and museum sit in a historical waterfront building that was once the fire hall and then the municipal office, and they share it today with the Alert Bay Visitor Centre. The museum shows local artifacts including a carved seine boat, a Mungo Martin carving, a net mending bench, a small totem pole and woven baskets, and there is a gift shop. A Summer Reading Program for Kids runs in the summer, with details only from the librarian, and the site describes no tour, class visit or group booking of any kind.
venue.address: 116 Fir Street, Alert Bay, BC V0N 1A0
venue.hours_notes: Open Tuesday to Saturday from 1 to 4. Closed Sunday and Monday.

programs.name: Museum and library visit
programs.description: The museum and gift shop are open to visitors during library hours, Tuesday to Saturday from 1 to 4. The site shows a sample of the artifacts on display: a carved seine boat, a Mungo Martin carving, a net mending bench, a small totem pole, a sunset with seine boat and woven baskets. No admission price, group rate, guided tour, minimum age, group size or booking route is published anywhere on the site, so a group visit has to be arranged by phone or email with the librarian.
programs.what_children_do: Look at the local history displays in the museum, among them a carved seine boat, a carving by Mungo Martin, a net mending bench, a small totem pole and woven baskets, then the gift shop and the library in the same building.
programs.our_note: The doors are only open from 1 to 4, Tuesday to Saturday, and the building is out on Cormorant Island, so the trip has to be built around a narrow afternoon window. Nothing on the site is written for groups, so phone or email first and ask what a group of children can actually do there.
programs.practical_summary: The address, coordinates, phone, email and the 1 to 4 opening hours are published. Washrooms, somewhere to eat, parking, accessibility, whether there is a charge and whether groups need to book are not stated anywhere, so call before you plan the day.
programs.evidence: Visit our museum and gift shop showcasing our rich local history.
